name: refiner
description: Focus: work one feature of a model across its levels, card by card, and hand the work to an AI between rounds. The AI side runs as lanes in the model: a hand-over request becomes a refinement, structure or ground pass run by an agent, or a read-only coder run through the headless-agent runner, both through the Agentic-Nets MCP server, with every run recorded. Its prompts and coder profiles are tokens you can edit; an upgrade keeps an edited one. Guided rounds ask up to ten adaptive questions about one topic across layers, then refine definitions and topology from sealed answers with resumable operation receipts.
author: AgenticNetOS

stores.description: Hand-over requests: a pass the person asked the AI to run; consumed by the lane when it runs
What each run did: the agent's report (summary, changes, questions, passId)

Where the coder works: the root folder of the model's sources on the executor, the coder profile (profileId and a base64 snapshot of it, profileB64), an optional model and the MCP server the coder reports to with the tools it may call there; append-only, the newest record wins and the coder lanes read it

Coder profiles (headless-agent format: profileId, family, mode, command, allowed tools); seeded with Claude Code read-only. Focus reads sources only: a profile whose mode is not read-only is refused. Edit a profile or add one; an upgrade replaces only a profile you never edited

The method's prompts, one token per promptId: rules (shared by every coder task), the coder kinds (refinement, structure, ground, look, explain, check, draft, diff) and refinement-pass (the agent lane's prompt). {{name}} placeholders are filled by the hand-over. Edit a prompt; an upgrade keeps it
Coder tasks waiting: the composed prompt per requestId; the coder lanes consume them
What each coder run reported: requestId, ok, exit code and the runner's JSON (profile, mode, the CODER_RESULT report, the answer's tail, stderr)
Persistent guided interviews, exact questions and answers, sealed inputs, operation receipts and resumable progress.
Validated round tasks for a read-only headless CLI; no MCP credentials.
Commands invoking the shared headless-agent runner.
Provider-independent structured round results, correlated by requestId.

actions.name: request
actions.description: Hand the focus work over to the AI: a refinement pass (apply answers and briefs, prepare the next questions), a structure pass (settle the AI's cards from the sources) or a ground pass (check the levels against the sources), optionally limited to a focus scope and a subject. One record per requestId; the lane t-refiner-pass consumes it. Kinds that read the sources (structure, ground, look, explain, check, draft, diff) are delegated to the coder lanes (action delegate).

modelId.description: The model the pass runs on; the lane passes it to every MCP call

scope.description: A focus scope (domain:<d>, tag:<t>, net:<session::net>); empty for the whole model

subject.description: One subject to concentrate on first

note.description: What the person wants from this pass, in their words

runner.description: agent: the lane t-refiner-pass (no sources needed); coder: the coder lanes (read the sources)

status.description: requested: waiting for t-refiner-pass; delegated: handed to the coder lanes

card.description: The Focus card the request came from (kind, title, detail, question)

actions.name: configure
actions.description: Set where and with what the coder works: the root folder of the model's sources on the executor (a path, ~ allowed), the coder profile (profileId from the coders store; the hand-over records a snapshot in profileB64), an optional model and the MCP server's URL (mcpUrl, set by the hand-over). Append-only; the newest record wins.

coder.description: Deprecated since 1.4.0 (profileId replaces it): claude or codex

profileId.description: A profile of the coders store (default claude-code-read-only)

profileB64.description: The profile's data as base64-encoded JSON, recorded by the hand-over (what the coder lanes run)

mcpUrl.description: The MCP server the coder reports to, recorded by the hand-over

mcpTools.description: The MCP tools the coder may call, comma separated, recorded by the hand-over

actions.name: delegate
actions.description: Hand one task to the coder: the prompt the hand-over composed from the prompt tokens. The coder lanes take it with the newest config (folder, profile, MCP server); a request cannot choose either. One record per requestId; the run's report lands in coder-results under the same requestId.

prompt.description: The task; it ends by asking for one line CODER_RESULT: {json}

purpose.description: The kind (structure, ground, look, explain, check, draft, diff, refinement)

actions.name: createRound
actions.description: Create the canonical guided-round token. Lifecycle changes use the version-checked Focus round service.

actions.name: dispatchRound
actions.description: Queue a validated guided-round command. Called by the round service with a frozen read-only profile and no MCP connection.

agentProtocol.summary: The review method's passes and question rounds as MCP prompts; each names the tools it needs.

prompts.name: structure-pass
prompts.title: Settle the model's structural cards from the sources, without the person
prompts.description: Take the cards meant for the AI (nothing refines this, draft definitions, failed refinements, nets below nothing, never confirmed) and settle each by reading the sources; ask the person only what the sources cannot tell

arguments.name: scope
arguments.description: A level id, a net key (session::net), or a focus scope (domain:<d>, tag:<t>, net:<session::net>); default: the whole model

arguments.name: count
arguments.description: How many cards to settle this pass (default 20)

prompts.text:
Run a structure pass{{#model}} in model "{{model}}" (pass model:"{{model}}" on every call){{/model}} on {{#scope}}{{scope}}{{/scope}}{{^scope}}the whole model{{/scope}}, {{#count}}{{count}}{{/count}}{{^count}}20{{/count}} cards at most. These cards are the model's own housekeeping; the person decides only what the sources cannot settle.

1. Read: refine_model { {{#scope=~^(domain|tag|net|any):}}scope:"{{scope}}", {{/scope}}{{#scope=~^[^:]+::}}net:"{{scope}}", {{/scope}}{{#scope=~^[^:]+$}}level:"{{scope}}", {{/scope}}for:"model"} for the structural cards{{#scope=~^(domain|tag|net|any):}} (they include one scope-gap card per level the scope's chain passes without a net of its own){{/scope}}; explore_model for the hierarchy; for each card get_net_definition and read the sources the definition references (files, documents, data) yourself.
2. Settle each card from what you read: "nothing refines this" becomes a child definition when the sources show a step with its own inner structure (update_net_definition {action:"create"} under the parent element, status draft, interactions from the sources, references to them), a confirmation with note "known gap" when something is there you cannot describe yet, or a confirmation with note "as simple as it looks" when the step is one thing. A draft definition is filled from the sources (update_net_definition, then status ready) or deleted when nothing realizes it. A failed refinement is repaired (ports, missing target) or flagged wrong with the evidence. A net below nothing gets its parent (organize) or an explains relation, or is flagged. A never-confirmed net is confirmed at the sourceHash when its claims hold in the sources, flagged (wrong, unclear, unmeasured) with evidence when they do not.
{{#scope=~^(domain|tag|net|any):}}2b. Look around {{scope}} before asking anything: focus_scope {scope:"{{scope}}"} lists its nets per level, the nets around it with how each connects, and the gaps (levels its chain passes without a net of its own). For each open gap decide from the sources and from the other features on that level (the gap's examples): the scope needs its own net there (update_net_definition {action:"create"} on that level, domain and tags of the scope, the parent element its chain passes, status draft), the level is covered by a net in its chain (curate_model {action:"confirm", subjectKey: the gap's subjectKey, notes:"covered by <net>: <why>"}), or it is not needed (confirm with notes "not needed: <why>"); only when neither the sources nor the neighbours settle it, ask the person on the gap's subjectKey. For each neighbour with cards (parent, child, depends-on and its inverse, explains, references, shares-place) read its definition and open decisions: a change or an open question there that affects the scope becomes a flag on the scope's net (level-above-changed / level-below-changed / unclear) or a question with the neighbour as evidence. Derive from the other features: what they have that the scope lacks on the same level (acceptance criteria, error states, rules, a place they share, a child net they refine) is a candidate gap; raise it with evidence from both sides, never silently copy it.
{{/scope}}3. Ask only what the sources cannot tell: a reason, an intent, a choice between two readings. Then curate_model {action:"ask", evidence, reasoning, options} as in a question round.
4. Record the pass: curate_model {action:"pass", consumedUntil: focus_digest's until, scope:"{{#scope=~^(domain|tag|net|any):}}focus:<focus_scope's scope>{{/scope}}{{#scope=~^[^:]+(::|$)}}structure:{{scope}}{{/scope}}{{^scope}}structure:model{{/scope}}", summary, changes, questions}. Report what was settled per kind and what went to the person. Never push, never start anything on a schedule.

prompts.name: ground-model
prompts.title: Extract the truth from the bottom level and check every level above
prompts.description: Walk the bottom level (code, documents, data), read its sources, and check each level above against them: confirm what holds, correct what is mechanical, ask the person where the levels and the sources disagree

arguments.name: level
arguments.description: The bottom level id (default: the lowest level)

arguments.name: net
arguments.description: One bottom net (session::net) instead of the whole level

arguments.name: policy
arguments.description: sources-win: correct the levels silently where the sources clearly decide; ask: every divergence becomes a card (default ask)

prompts.text:
Ground the model{{#model}} in model "{{model}}" (pass model:"{{model}}" on every call){{/model}}: the bottom level is where the model touches the domain's own material (for software the code, for a process its documents, for a product its measurements). Extract what is true there and carry it up through every level, so the abstractions say what the material does.

1. Read: ground_model { {{#level}}level:"{{level}}" {{/level}}{{#net}}net:"{{net}}" {{/net}}} for the chains: every bottom net with the nets above it, each node with its claims (description, interactions, acceptance), its references, its definition revision and its confirmation (revision, sourceHash, when). If the model is built from a specification, run its checker and its grounding tool first (they settle the mechanical part: references exist and contain what they claim, parameters hold their values) and take their cards and flags as given.
2. For each chain, bottom-up: read the bottom node's referenced sources yourself. Then for every node above it compare each claim with what you read. Three outcomes. Agree: curate_model {action:"confirm", subjectKey, subjectRevision, sourceHash, notes: what was checked}. Mechanical divergence (a renamed symbol, a changed value or count, a moved file): {{#policy=~^sources-win$}}correct the level (update_net_definition or the specification plus a rebuild), then confirm it{{/policy}}{{^policy=~^sources-win$}}correct the level when the sources clearly decide it (update_net_definition or the specification plus a rebuild), then confirm it; when the change could be a regression rather than the truth, treat it as a decision{{/policy}}. Decision divergence (the level says the product should do X, the sources do Y, and either could be the intended one): curate_model {action:"flag", flag:"contradiction", reason, evidence} on the node, and {action:"ask", subjectKey, header:"Sources differ", evidence: [what the level claims, what the sources do, file and line], reasoning: which one you believe is intended and why, options: [{keep-level: keep the level as written, the sources must change}, {adopt-sources: the sources are right, the level changes}, {both: both need a change}], allowFreeText:true}. A chain whose upper nodes were confirmed before the bottom node (aboveConfirmedBeforeBottom) is checked first.
3. Never invent: a claim you cannot check against a source is flagged unmeasured, not confirmed. Carry a change down as well as up: when a level changes, the nets it refines are re-checked.
4. Record the pass: curate_model {action:"pass", consumedUntil: focus_digest's until, scope:"ground:{{#level}}{{level}}{{/level}}{{^level}}bottom{{/level}}", summary, changes: [nodes confirmed, nodes corrected], questions: [cards raised]}. Report per chain: agreed, corrected, asked. Never push.

prompts.name: refinement-pass
prompts.title: Apply what the person answered, top-down, and prepare the next focus session
prompts.description: Read the digest since the last pass, revise every layer above the realization that the answers touch, resolve what is settled, raise the next questions and record the pass

arguments.name: scope
arguments.description: A level id, a persona, a net key, or a focus scope (domain:<d>, tag:<t>, net:<session::net>: one feature across its levels) to limit the pass; default: the whole model

arguments.name: since
arguments.description: ISO-8601 instant to start from; default: the last recorded pass

prompts.text:
Run a refinement pass{{#model}} in model "{{model}}" (pass model:"{{model}}" on every call){{/model}}{{#scope}} limited to {{scope}}{{/scope}}. Focus sessions (the person answers cards in the Focus application or here) and refinement passes (this) alternate as often as needed; implementation is a separate step later (prompt implement-from-model). The goal of a pass is the layers above the realization (the code, the process, the document, whatever the lowest level is): after it, every definition the answers touched says what the person meant, and the next focus session asks only what nobody can derive.

1. Read: focus_digest { {{#since}}since:"{{since}}", {{/since}}{{#scope=~^(domain|tag|net|any):}}scope:"{{scope}}"{{/scope}}{{#scope=~^[^:]+::}}scope:"{{scope}}"{{/scope}}{{#scope=~^[^:]+$}}level:"{{scope}}"{{/scope}}} for what was answered, confirmed, flagged, resolved and deferred since the last pass, grouped by level and subject, the person's BRIEFS (notes of noteKind brief: what they said about a subject in their own words, the planning input; derive the subject's definition from a brief, nothing invented, and carry the change down and up), plus the questions still open and the person's own questions (ownQuestions: answer each by changing the model or by asking back with curate_model {action:"ask", requestId}); an answer with intent "revise" carries the person's better wording in revisedQuestion: ask it again with supersedes; note the digest's `until`. explore_model for the hierarchy and the levels in order. get_net_definition for every subject in the digest (description, interactions, acceptance, references, questions, curation).
2. Apply top-down, level by level from the highest: for each subject, read its answers and marks together. A "right" confirms the definition as it is (nothing to change; keep the confirmation). A "partly" or "wrong" with the person's words changes the definition: revise description, interactions and acceptance with update_net_definition (or the specification file plus a rebuild when the model is spec-built; then confirm the rebuilt revision at the current sourceHash), and carry the change DOWN: every child net whose definition contradicts the new wording is revised or flagged level-above-changed, and the parent element is checked (level-below-changed when a child's answer changes what the parent claims). A request to refine here becomes a child definition (update_net_definition {action:"create"} with the parent element, status draft) with the ports the parent's element implies. Free text that is a reason nobody could derive goes into the definition's interactions or the model's context net, never lost. Resolve every flag the change settles (curate_model {action:"resolve", how:"changed"}); leave open what still needs the person.
3. Check: reread get_net_definition and explore_model on what you changed (or run the specification checker when the model is spec-built); the catalogue must verify every refinement you touched (ports, targets). Nothing is started that spends quota on a schedule.
{{#scope=~^(domain|tag|net|any):}}3b. Stay inside the focus, but look around {{scope}} before asking anything: focus_scope {scope:"{{scope}}"} lists its nets per level, the nets around it with how each connects, and the gaps (levels its chain passes without a net of its own). For each open gap decide from the sources and from the other features on that level (the gap's examples): the scope needs its own net there (update_net_definition {action:"create"} on that level, domain and tags of the scope, the parent element its chain passes, status draft), the level is covered by a net in its chain (curate_model {action:"confirm", subjectKey: the gap's subjectKey, notes:"covered by <net>: <why>"}), or it is not needed (confirm with notes "not needed: <why>"); only when neither the sources nor the neighbours settle it, ask the person on the gap's subjectKey. For each neighbour with cards (parent, child, depends-on and its inverse, explains, references, shares-place) read its definition and open decisions: a change or an open question there that affects the scope becomes a flag on the scope's net (level-above-changed / level-below-changed / unclear) or a question with the neighbour as evidence. Derive from the other features: what they have that the scope lacks on the same level (acceptance criteria, error states, rules, a place they share, a child net they refine) is a candidate gap; raise it with evidence from both sides, never silently copy it.
{{/scope}}3c. Summarize for the person: for every subject with a brief or an answer, curate_model {action:"note", noteKind:"summary", subjectKey, text} with what you understood, what you changed (revision) and what stays open, in 3 to 8 sentences; Focus shows it in the subject's thread. Offer analogies: what the analogous subjects on the same level decided becomes an option of the next question.
4. Raise the next questions about the thing itself (what it should do, which rule, which value, which trade-off), not about the nets: for every change, ask what it opens (the next lower level first), with curate_model {action:"ask", subjectKey, question, header, evidence, reasoning, options, subjectRevision}. Every card carries substance the person can argue with: evidence = what you read or measured, one item each with its finding (file and line, document, number, the person's earlier words); reasoning = why the question matters, the trade-off between the options, which one you recommend and why; options = two to four, each with a description of its consequence, exactly one recommended; allowFreeText true. A question without evidence and reasoning is not asked. Prefer decide / choose / explain kinds; at most {{#scope}}5{{/scope}}{{^scope}}10{{/scope}} new questions, the rest waits for the next pass. Deferred subjects stay untouched until their date.
5. Record the pass: curate_model {action:"pass", consumedUntil: the digest's until, scope{{#scope=~^(domain|tag|net|any):}} (exactly focus_scope's passScope, so the next digest of this focus starts after it and the whole model still sees the answers){{/scope}}, summary, answers: count consumed, changes: [...], questions: [promptIds raised], by: you}. Report here: per level what changed, what was resolved, what was asked, what stays open and why; name the definitions revised by key. Never push. (Every step is a tool call; an MCP client can run the pass without this prompt and without a server-side LLM.)

prompts.name: implement-from-model
prompts.title: Realize a net of the lowest layer from its definition
prompts.description: A separate step after focus and refinement: turn one confirmed lowest-layer net into work items or code through an interview here, never silently

arguments.name: net
arguments.description: The net to implement (session::net), normally on the lowest level above the code

arguments.name: output
arguments.description: cards (work items in a kanban application), code (edit the referenced sources), or plan (a written plan only); default: ask

prompts.text:
Implement {{net}}{{#model}} in model "{{model}}" (pass model:"{{model}}" on every call){{/model}} from its definition. This is the step AFTER focus and refinement: the layers above the realization are done when the net and its parents are confirmed and no open flag or question remains on them; implementation starts only then and only through this interview.

1. Readiness: get_net_definition for {{net}} and explore_model for its parents; review_model for its curation. If the net or a parent is unconfirmed, flagged or has open questions, stop and say what a focus session must settle first (refine_model {net:"{{net}}"} lists it). If the model is spec-built, name the specification entry.
2. Interview me, one question at a time, about what the definition leaves to the implementer: the output ({{#output}}{{output}}{{/output}}{{^output}}cards for a kanban application, code in the referenced sources, or a written plan{{/output}}), the boundary (which referenced sources may change, which may not), the order (which transition first), the acceptance that will be checked and how, and who reviews. Record each answer with curate_model {action:"ask", evidence, reasoning, options with descriptions and one recommended} + {action:"answer"} on subject "{{net}}" so the decisions and the arguments live in the model.
3. Produce exactly the agreed output: cards through the installed kanban application (application_action, one card per transition or per acceptance line, owner = the level's persona, the net key in the card), or code edits in the referenced sources with the net's acceptance as the test list, or a plan as a definition note. Never start a transition, a scheduled lane or a headless coder on your own; a command transition that triggers implementation is a later platform step and is not wired here.
4. Close the loop: confirm the net at the new sourceHash when sources changed (curate_model {action:"confirm", sourceHash}), flag the definition level-below-changed when the implementation taught something the definition did not say, and report what was produced, what was checked, what stays open.

prompts.name: question-round
prompts.title: Run a question round on a level or a net
prompts.description: Check what the model claims against its sources, ask the person what only they know, and record confirmations, flags and answers

arguments.name: scope
arguments.description: A level id or a net key (session::net); default: whatever needs the person most

arguments.name: count
arguments.description: How many questions to ask this round (default 5)

arguments.name: persona
arguments.description: The persona asking, when the model has one per level

prompts.text:
Run a question round{{#model}} in model "{{model}}" (pass model:"{{model}}" on every call){{/model}} {{#persona}}as the {{persona}}{{/persona}}{{^persona}}as the keeper of that level{{/persona}}, on {{#scope}}{{scope}}{{/scope}}{{^scope}}what needs me most{{/scope}}, {{#count}}{{count}}{{/count}}{{^count}}5{{/count}} questions at most. One question at a time; I answer here or in the Explorer.

1. Read: refine_model { {{#scope=~^(domain|tag|net|any):}}scope:"{{scope}}", {{/scope}}{{#scope=~^[^:]+::}}net:"{{scope}}", {{/scope}}{{#scope=~^[^:]+$}}level:"{{scope}}", {{/scope}}direction:"both"} for the worklist (looking down: transitions nothing refines, refinements that do not verify, definitions still open; looking up: nets below nothing; and the review: open flags, open questions, never confirmed), each item with a ready-made question; explore_model for the hierarchy; get_net_definition for the nets you will ask about (description, interactions, acceptance, references, questions already answered, curation). Never ask what an answered question already settled.
2. Check before asking (no LLM needed for most of it): every reference the definition names still exists and still contains what it claims; every parameter named still has that value; every transition at this level is refined below or named as a known gap; a confirmed net whose referenced sources changed since (sourceHash) is stale. If the model is built from a specification file, run its checker. Record each mechanical finding as a flag with a deterministic markId (application_action on "curation", action "flag", subjectKind net|element, subjectKey "<session>::<net>" or "<session>::<net>#<elementId>", flag, reason with the measured evidence, by = you). Resolve flags the check no longer finds (action "resolve", how "changed").
3. Ask only what you cannot find out: the reasons behind a rule, whether a description still describes what the person means (the code, the process, the rule, the document), a better name, whether a net is too coarse. Prefer these kinds: confirm ("the net says X, the sources do Y: right / partly / wrong / don't know"), choose (options), explain (free text, the most valuable kind), name, split-or-merge. Each question goes through curate_model {action:"ask", subjectKey, question, header, evidence, reasoning, options, subjectRevision} (the worklist's item.ask is a starting point; the subject kind and a promptId are derived) and carries substance: evidence = what you read or measured with its finding, reasoning = why it matters, the trade-off and your recommendation with the reason, options with a description each and one recommended. Show me the question here as well and wait for my answer before the next one.
4. Record each answer with curate_model {action:"answer", promptId, selected or text, respondedBy = the person}; add then:"confirm" (+ subjectKey, notes = their words) when the answer confirms the subject, or then:"flag" (+ flag, reason) when it refutes it. When it changes the model, change the specification and rebuild (or update_net_definition when the model is edited directly), then curate_model {action:"resolve"} the related flags. When the answer is a reason nobody could have derived, put it where the next reader finds it: the definition's interactions, a note on the confirmation, or the model's context net.
5. Report: what was confirmed, what was flagged, what changed, what stays open. Never push, never start anything that spends quota on a schedule. (Every step here is a tool call: an MCP client can run the whole round without this prompt and without a server-side LLM.)

workflow: suggest next round; wait for the person

mcp.reason: The review pass (t-refiner-pass) reads the model and writes summaries, notes and questions through the platform's MCP server, limited to these review tools. The coder's run lane (t-refiner-coder-run) receives the token itself; the headless-agent runner hands the coder only these tools. Neither builds, starts or deletes nets.
